text:
The Athletic says Zach Benson has arrived as a star, and our numbers mostly agree, with one glaring exception. He's 21, playing 20:07 a night (up from 15:53), on the ice for 71% of Buffalo's power-play time, and the Sabres have had 57.9% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him out there, nearly 11 points better than without him. Evolving-Hockey had him driving play in the 98th percentile among forwards last season. This is a real top-line role.

The exception is the goals. He has two on 7.8 expected, shooting 4.2% against a talent range closer to 11%. Few forwards in the league have a wider gap, and our wins-added numbers rank him near the bottom because of it. It's hard to see a player getting those looks staying this cold.

The assists have kept him afloat, 13 of them, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him exiting his own zone with possession 64% of the time. When the shooting turns, the line catches up quickly.
headline: Benson is a star with no goals to show
